$Comment: The Headless Horseman in the saddle on the hard ride, the form his hard fight (Hallows_Eve_Headless_Horseman_Encounter_Hard) opens with: Hallows_Eve_Headless_Horseman_Mounted written out again, as the game writes its own hard bosses, with more health, the hard name, the Hallows_Eve_Horseman_Hard_Mode effect, which makes what he swings and throws hit harder, and one attack the normal ride lacks: he hurls a lantern bomb (Root_Hallows_Eve_Horseman_Bomb) at a player within 18 blocks, but only after aiming at them for 3 seconds (RangedAttackAimingRange, the game's own flier aim tell, as its void eyes do: the template's Aim head motion keeps him turned on that player the whole time), then waits 2 to 3 seconds (RangedAttackPauseRange) before he aims again. He flies the same way, through the same Hallows_Eve_Horseman_Ride (CombatAdditionalBehaviorComponent): dives to fight low (1 to 3 blocks up), wide high swings around the graveyard, laps of its fountain, swoops and bomb passes, turning on the nearest player every 4 to 6 seconds unless his target is within TargetRange. MotionFlyMaxHeightAboveGround must clear the highest of the Ride's points (laps 7 up, swings 7 to 9, the climb point he makes for when something blocks him 10). The hard fight swaps him to Hallows_Eve_Headless_Horseman_HM on foot and his health carries across, so MaxHealth here must equal that role's. Fire hurts him at half (Hallows_Eve_Horseman_Fire_Ward), never shoved, DropList Empty since his reward is the Claims his fight pays. Any key the template does not declare makes the game refuse the whole role.
